subject: Service reliability measurement and temporary dashboard access - procurement inquiry
messages:
From: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@brightwave.io>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.example>, Procurement <procurement@brightwave.io>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Procurement questionnaire - metrics, alerts, and dashboard access

Hi Sergio,

Hope you’re well. Procurement at Brightwave has a short set of SLO/SLA questions we need to clear before we finalize the order. I’ve attached our standard questionnaire (procurement_slo_questionnaire.pdf). Key asks we need answers for are:

- How do you compute "uptime" for Redwood-hosted models? Measurement window (calendar month/rolling 30d)?
- What latency metrics are available (p50/p95/p99, per-model or aggregate)? Are they measured server-side only or end-to-end (including network)?
- What monitoring stack do you use and what retention do you provide for production telemetry?
- What alerting thresholds map to customer-visible SLAs and what is the on-call/escalation flow?
- Can Brightwave be granted read-only access to a dashboard (Grafana) and/or receive a one-time trimmed export of telemetry for onboarding validation? We only need access for ~90 days.
- In the event of an outage, how are credits calculated and who validates the measurement?

We’ll need this answered by EOD next Tuesday to keep our procurement timeline. If you prefer, we can set a 30-minute call.

Thanks,
Morgan Lee
Contracts Manager, Brightwave

Attachments: procurement_slo_questionnaire.pdf

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.example>
To: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@brightwave.io>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.example>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.example>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire - metrics, alerts, and dashboard access

Morgan — thanks for the clear list. I’ve answered the questions below inline to speed things up. I’m happy to hop on a short call if you want to walk through anything. I’ve also attached a short brief and a temporary Grafana invite.

1) How we compute uptime
- Uptime is measured as the proportion of successful "request/response" cycles over a calendar month (UTC). Internal definition: success = 2xx response from the inference service and model token streaming completes without server-side errors. We exclude scheduled maintenance windows that were communicated in advance.
- SLO baseline we publish: 99.9% monthly availability for hosted API endpoints (route-level). We provide per-route historical availability on request.

2) Latency metrics
- We publish p50, p95, p99 latency for synchronous text generation and embedding routes. Latencies are server-side (time from request arrival at the edge to final model response emission). If you require end-to-end measurements that include client-network time, we can instrument a lightweight synthetic probe for validation during onboarding.

3) Monitoring stack & retention
- Primary telemetry: Prometheus + Grafana for metrics, Loki for short-term logs, and a long-term cold store (S3) for trimmed telemetry exports.
- Production metrics retention: 90 days at full resolution; aggregated 1y at daily rollups.

4) Alerting thresholds & escalation
- We map alerts to internal SLO tiers: "service degraded" (availability < 99.5% rolling 1h), "service impaired" (availability < 99% rolling 15m), and "service down" (no successful requests for 5+ minutes). High-severity incidents page on-call and notify account engineering if customer routes are impacted.
- Incident contact: after alert firing, our on-call SRE triages within 15 minutes; account engineering and customer success are notified automatically for severity P1/P0 incidents.

5) Dashboard access & telemetry export
- We can grant a read-only Grafana invite scoped to the routes you specify. Typical access window we grant for onboarding is 60–90 days. The Grafana invite is temporary and IP-restricted where requested. I’ll send the invite link as an attachment.
- For procurement validation we can also provide a one-time trimmed telemetry export (no raw user prompts) covering the requested interval. For raw logs or PII-containing artifacts we require an NDA and a data access request.

6) SLA credits & measurement validation
- Credits are calculated based on % below the monthly uptime SLO; our SLA has a standard credit schedule (see attached brief). Measurements used for credits are from our primary telemetry pipeline; customers may request a review within 30 days.

Next steps:
- I attached a short PDF that summarizes the above (slo-measurement-brief.pdf) and a temporary invite (grafana-invite.txt). If Brightwave wants the 90-day Grafana access I can provision that once we confirm scope (routes + read-only users).

Let me know if you want a 30-min call tomorrow.

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: slo-measurement-brief.pdf, grafana-invite.txt

From: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@brightwave.io>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@brightwave.io>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2026 13:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire - metrics, alerts, and dashboard access

Thanks Sergio — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups before we finish the questionnaire: 

- For the 60–90 day Grafana access, can you restrict it to only the production routes used in our account and limit IP addresses to our corporate VPN?
- We need a temporary carve-out for our internal compliance team: during the first 30 days of integration we cannot receive push alerts from Redwood on P1 unless we explicitly sign off (we’ll still review incident postmortems). Is Redwood able to support a temporary mute for customer-originating alert notifications (Redwood would still be on-call internally)?
- For SLA credits, can you confirm whether credit amounts are pro-rata and whether we can elect to receive credit as invoice reduction vs. account credit?

If you can answer these three items I think Procurement can sign off.

—Morgan

Sergio — quick internal note and approval for the path forward.

- Grafana: we can scope the read-only dashboard to specific routes and apply an IP allowlist. Security will issue a time-limited invite (60 days default, extendable to 90 with justification). We’ll attach the invite to the procurement packet and record the access in the entitlement tracker.
- Alerts: we can support a customer-requested mute for external push notifications for the first 30 days. Redwood will remain on-call and will continue internal paging for P0/P1 events. The mute will be documented in the customer record and requires a signed acknowledgement that Brightwave will not receive automatic push notifications during the carve-out window.
- Credits: credits are pro-rata against the monthly invoice. Brightwave can elect invoice reduction or account credit; we’ll reflect that preference on the order form.

Action items: Sergio — provision Grafana invite scoped to routes: brightwave-prod-chat, brightwave-prod-embeddings; set IP allowlist to 52.78.11.0/24 plus their corporate VPN range once provided; create trimmed telemetry export for the last 7 days excluding any raw prompts and place in secure S3 for download. I’ll sign off on the exception once the access is provisioned and the acknowledgment form is returned.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Sr. Product Manager, Reliability
